original_question: Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, let u ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n, R^{n+1}), and set b = H(u) ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n) ∩ L^∞(R^n). Determine the largest subspace V ⊂ H^1(R^n) for which the commutator [b, I] maps V to L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n) or to W^{1,1}(R^n), the commutators [b, R_α] map V to L^1(R^n), the Jacobian form du^1 ∧ ... ∧ du^n admits an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, and whether the answers change when u is assumed to solve an H-system.
target_in_paper: Problem 4.1 (parts (a)–(d)) in Section 4.1 of Schikorra & Strzelecki, arXiv:1606.07891
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the setting H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, u∈W^{1,n}(R^n,R^{n+1}), b=H(u)∈W^{1,n}(R^n)∩L^∞(R^n), the search for a largest subspace V⊂H^1(R^n) on which the commutator [b,I] maps V to L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n) or to W^{1,1}(R^n), the analogous question for [b,R_α]:V→L^1(R^n), whether the Jacobian form du^1∧…∧du^n admits an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, and whether the answers change when u solves an H-system.
missing_details: Definition of the Riesz potential operator I: I f(x)=∫_{R^n}K(x−y)f(y)dy with K(x)=c_n x/|x|^n
Precise identification that H^1(R^n) is the real Hardy space and W^{1,1}(R^n) the Sobolev space
Definition of the Riesz transforms R_α for α=1,…,n
Explicit statement of the question "Does V contain the n×n minors of the Jacobian matrix Du?" as in parts (a) and (b)
Definition of b-atoms: standard Hardy atoms orthogonal to the function b
Quantification that V is a linear subspace of H^1(R^n) and that α ranges over 1,…,n
refined_question: Let n≥2, H:R^{n+1}→R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u:R^n→R^{n+1} satisfy u∈W^{1,n}(R^n,R^{n+1}), b:=H∘u∈W^{1,n}(R^n)∩L^∞(R^n). Denote by I the Riesz potential I f(x)=∫_{R^n}c_n(x−y)/|x−y|^n f(y)dy mapping H^1(R^n)→L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n), and by R_α the α-th Riesz transform on R^n, α=1,…,n. (a) What is the largest subspace V⊂H^1(R^n) such that the commutator [b,I]:V→L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n) extends boundedly? What is the answer if L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n) is replaced by W^{1,1}(R^n)? In either case, does this V necessarily contain all n×n minors of the Jacobian Du? (b) What is the largest V⊂H^1(R^n) such that, for each α=1,…,n, the commutator [b,R_α]:V→L^1(R^n) is bounded? Does V contain all n×n minors of Du? (c) Does the n-form du^1∧…∧du^n admit an atomic decomposition in H^1(R^n) with atoms that are orthogonal to b (so-called b-atoms)? (d) If u furthermore is a weak solution of the H-system div(|∇u|^{n−2}∇u)=H(u)Ju, do the answers to (a)–(c) change?
justification: This question precisely restates Problem 4.1 (parts (a)–(d)) from the paper, incorporating all required definitions and quantifications to be fully self-contained and faithful to the paper's intent.
